groups.title: Authentication Concepts
groups.question: You are adding login to your Next.js app with GitHub and email-password options, and the whole /dashboard area must be private. Explain the auth flows, session choices and how you protect routes.

followUps.OAuth flow and credential-based authenti: How does OAuth login differ from a credentials provider?
followUps.Sessions vs JWT token strategies: What are the trade-offs between database sessions and JWT sessions?
followUps.Protecting routes with middleware-based: Why protect routes in middleware, and is that enough?

evidence.text: OAuth sends the user to a provider like GitHub, which confirms who they are.
A credentials provider checks a username and password in your own app.
With credentials, you are responsible for storing and protecting passwords safely.

notEnough: Only saying both log users in.

evidence.text: Database sessions store a session record and send its id in a cookie.
JWT sessions put the session data in a signed token.
Database sessions are easy to revoke but need lookups; JWTs avoid lookups but are hard to revoke early.

notEnough: Only saying one uses a database.

evidence.text: Middleware runs before the request reaches a page.
It redirects unauthenticated users in one central place.
Data access in pages and actions must still check the session.

groups.title: Auth.js Integration Patterns
groups.question: You want users to stay signed in across devices and to show their name in both server and client components. Explain how Auth.js stores and exposes sessions.

followUps.Prisma adapter for persisting sessions t: What does the Prisma adapter store?
followUps.Reading session server-side and client-s: When do you use auth() and when useSession?

evidence.text: It stores users, accounts and sessions in your database.
It needs specific models added to the Prisma schema.
Stored sessions support looking up users and managing several devices.

notEnough: Only saying it connects to Prisma.

evidence.text: auth() reads the session in server components and actions.
useSession reads it in client components.
Reading it on the server avoids extra client requests and loading flashes.

groups.title: Auth.js Setup
groups.question: You are setting up Auth.js in a fresh Next.js app with GitHub login. Explain the configuration and the secrets it needs.

What goes in auth.ts and the auth route handler?
followUps.Environment variables for OAuth credenti: Which environment variables does it need and why?

evidence.text: auth.ts configures providers and exports auth, signIn and signOut.
A catch-all route under api/auth handles the auth requests.
All auth settings live in one file.
Each OAuth provider needs a client id and secret from its developer console.
AUTH_SECRET is a random string used to sign and encrypt tokens.
These stay in environment variables and are never committed.

notEnough: Only saying you set env vars.

groups.title: Route and Action Protection
groups.question: A user who is not logged in manages to delete a post by calling a server action directly, and you also need an admin-only page. Explain how you would secure actions and roles.

followUps.Protecting server actions by checking se: Why must every server action check the session itself?
followUps.Role-based access control with session c: How would you add a role to the session and enforce it?
followUps.Configuring sign-in and sign-out UI flow: How do you customise sign-in and sign-out flows?

evidence.text: Server actions can be called directly, not only from your UI.
Each action calls auth() and refuses if there is no session.
Hiding a button in the UI does not stop the request.

misconceptions.text: Says hiding the delete button is enough to protect the action.

evidence.text: The jwt and session callbacks add custom fields like role.
Middleware or actions check the role before allowing access.
Users without the role get a forbidden response.
Custom sign-in pages are set through the pages option.
signIn and signOut can be called from server actions.
Redirects send users to the right page afterwards.

notEnough: Only saying Auth.js has default pages.
